sentences.text:
The case originated from the complaint of the 2nd respondent against petitioners 1 to 4 under Section 42(5) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ("the FSS Act" for short) alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 26(1), 26(2)(i), 27, 59(i)
and Section 3(1)(zz)(iii) and 3(1)(zz)(x) of the FSS Act.
Thereafter, sampling was done and a sample was sent in Form VI to the Food Analyst.
After analysis Form VIIA report was submitted to the Designated Officer, Ernakulam as per which the sample contained Rodent Excreta (Contamination) which is injurious to health.

Therefore, it was found that the food articles are unsafe as per 3(1)(zz)(iii) and 3(1)(zz)(x) of the FSS Act and that the sample doesn't conform to the standards of coriander under the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Addictives) Regulations, 2011 and is therefore substandard as per Section 3.1(zx) of FSS Act.

sentences.text: Petitioners 2 to 4, being the Directors of the said company, are also liable for the said offence as they have not submitted their nomination as per the FSS Act and thereby the accused persons 2025:KER:65144 have together committed the aforesaid offences.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the complaint and further proceedings are liable to be quashed, since the prosecution of the petitioners, in their alleged capacity as Directors of the Food Manufacturer, M/s.Moolans Exports (India) Private Limited, is an abuse of process, since the company is not made an accused.

In support of the argument, reference is made to Section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act dealing with vicarious liability of the Directors of the accused company and reliance is placed on the decision of the Apex Court in Aneeta Hada v. Godfather Travels and Tours Private Limited [(2012) 5 SCC 661].

sentences.text: It is submitted that in the case at hand, the report of the Food Analyst was issued as early as on 05.03.2020, but the Designated Officer had forwarded the request for sanction to 2025:KER:65144 initiate prosecution only on 11.08.2020.

It is pointed out that as per Section 42(3) of the FSS Act,
the Designated Officer, after scrutiny of the report of the Food Analyst, has to decide whether the contravention is punishable with imprisonment or only fine and in case the contravention is punishable with imprisonment, send recommendations within 14 days to the Commissioner of Food Mary Rocky vs State Of Kerala on 13 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177596435/

sentences.text: Safety for sanctioning the prosecution.
According to the counsel, the unexplained delay from the part of the Designated Officer has rendered the prosecution illegal.
4. I heard the Additional Director General of Prosecution also.
5. A perusal of the complaint reveals that the 1 st petitioner is arrayed in his capacity as the Food Business Operator and the other petitioners, as Directors of the company.
Surprisingly, the manufacturer, viz; the company, is not made an accused.

In the FSS Act, offences by companies is dealt with in Section 66, extracted below;
2025:KER:65144 "66. Offences by companies.-

(1) Where an offence under this Act which has been committed by a company, every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly:
Provided that where a company has different establishments or branches or different units in any establishment or branch, the concerned Head or the person in-charge of such establishment, branch, unit nominated by the company as responsible for food safety shall be liable for contravention in respect of such establishment, branch or unit:
Provided further that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act, if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company and it is proved that the offence has been committed with the consent or connivance of or is attributable to any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary or other officer of the company, such director, manager, secretary or other officer shall also be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. "
6. In Aneeta Hada (supra), after considering the vicarious liability of Directors of a company, with reference to Section 141 of the N.I.Act which is pari materia with Section 66 of the FSS Act, the Apex Court has held that for maintaining 2025:KER:65144 the prosecution, arraigning the company as an accused is imperative and the Directors cannot be prosecuted without the company being arrayed as an accused.
In Maruti Prasad Panda (supra)the Punjab and Haryana High Court has held the prosecution under the FSS Act to be illegal without the company being arraigned as an accused.
